P.note: Glossy blue lens artwork is a strong acrylic object, but the card reads as pale frosted white and the queue runs off the bottom of the 800px page, cutting the third row and hiding the fourth.

Q.note: The strongest Frutiger Aero read, with saturated blue sky, glossy green play orb and electric green hills, and the whole card fits the viewport, though the drifting bubbles are a familiar cliche and white queue text is weak on the pale rows.

R.note: The blade-textured electric green grass is convincing, but the artwork is a blurry blue blob that turns muddy against the blue sky and the card overflows the bottom of the page.

S.note: The whole card fits cleanly with four legible queue rows, a blue-tinted acrylic body with internal light and a hyperreal green grass field, though the blue-on-blue artwork is a little low in contrast and a faint ghost layer sits above the artwork.

T.note: The card is blue acrylic that fits the viewport and the artwork is well crafted, but the central play button visibly shows the play triangle and pause bars stacked at once, a clear rendering bug.

U.note: The blue acrylic card and glossy scene art are cohesive, but the card runs off the bottom of the page so only one up-next row is visible.
